CeilingShown.description:
The greyed quartered-Kelly ceiling, and the words it is always shown under.

A ceiling, never a size. The only number that sets a size is the reader's own
risk budget. **Zero and absent are different answers** and this shape says
which: a fraction of zero means the arithmetic ran and came out at nothing to
put on; nothing at all means there was no edge to run it on.

at.description: The likelihood it was worked out at: the unfavourable end of the model's range.

fraction.description: The share of capital, quartered, at the unfavourable end of the model's range.

sentence.description: Why the answer is zero, or why it is absent. Nothing where a fraction came out.
sentence.title: Sentence

taken_by.description: Which side of the venue's book it was worked out for.
taken_by.title: Taken By

warning.description: The words the number is always shown under.
warning.title: Warning

Conditions.description:
The computed lists, each row carrying what it rests on.

These are the conditions the legs above hold under: what carries them, what
takes the reader out, what to watch and by when, what cannot be watched for,
the tails, and any shock the reader placed.

carried_by.description: The claims whose arrows carry most of the hypothesis's effect on the ending.
carried_by.title: Carried By

shocks.description: Suppositions the reader placed, each with no probability.
shocks.title: Shocks

tails.description: Claims that are unlikely and would hurt, ranked by harm and never averaged.
tails.title: Tails

takes_you_out.description: The claims over-represented in the worlds where the stop went first.

unhedgeable.description: What is adverse and cannot be watched for, each with its reason.
unhedgeable.title: Unhedgeable

watch.description: What is adverse, resolves before the ending, and can be seen by anybody.
watch.title: Watch

Conditions.title: Conditions

Figure.description:
One number on the card, with who it belongs to and where it came from.

The card holds no bare numbers. A figure cannot be built without an owner, so
no screen and no document can print one without being handed the owner in the
same breath — which is the shape this repository prefers to a rule a renderer
has to remember.

`lo` and `hi` are the range around the number where one exists: the model's
own stated range on a likelihood, or the interval on a measured share. They
are absent where no range was stated, which is different from a range of zero
width.

about.description: What the number is, in plain words a reader needs no other page to follow.
about.title: About

hi.description: The top of that range. Absent together with `lo`.
hi.title: Hi

kind.description: What the number is, which decides how it is written: a likelihood and a share carry a guard word at each end, a move keeps its two figures however small, and a price, a count and a day are written as they are.
kind.title: Kind

lo.description: The bottom of the range around this number, where one was stated.
lo.title: Lo

owner.description: Whose number this is: the reader's, the model's, a venue's, or a computation over the drawn worlds. Exactly one of the four, and never a merge.
owner.title: Owner

source.description: Where it came from, where that is not obvious from the owner: the venue and the day a price was read, the sample a share was taken over, the rule a ranking used. Nothing at all for a number the reader typed.
source.title: Source

value.description: The number itself, at full precision. A rendering rounds.
value.title: Value

Figure.title: Figure

Hypothesis.description: The claim the map starts from.
Hypothesis.title: Hypothesis

Leg.description:
One position, with everything a reader of this document needs about it.

A leg is complete on its own: what is traded, which way, what the model says,
what a venue charges, the two edges or the named refusal, the break-even, the
size the reader's own risk budget implies, and the greyed ceiling with its
label attached. A program that reads a leg should not have to look anywhere
else to know what it may and may not do with the numbers in it.

One leg is what this version builds, because one position is what the reader
holds. The field is a list so that two positions are two legs rather than a
different document.

ceiling.description: The greyed quartered-Kelly ceiling, carried as a value with its label attached, so a program that reads the number reads *never size to this* with it.

claim.description: That ending's claim, in one sentence.
claim.title: Claim

contract_id.description: The venue's own identifier for that contract.
contract_id.title: Contract Id

contract_side.description: Which outcome of the contract the ending takes.
contract_side.title: Contract Side

ending.description: The ending this leg is on.
ending.title: Ending

instrument.description: What is bought or sold, named the way its venue names it.
instrument.title: Instrument

priced_in.description: The model's number, a venue's two prices and the two edges — or the named refusal and the break-even that stands where no edge could be built.
priced_in.title: Priced In

resolution_test.description: The test that settles it, word for word.
resolution_test.title: Resolution Test

resolves.description: The day the ending's own claim is judged.
resolves.title: Resolves

side.description: Which way the trade is pointed.
side.title: Side

size.description: The share of capital the reader's own risk budget implies. Their rule's arithmetic, and never a recommendation.

trades.description: Whether it names something traded whose price moves, or a contract.
trades.title: Trades

venue.description: The venue, where the ending names a contract.
venue.title: Venue

MixtureShown.description:
How a supposed reading relates to the unsupposed one — an explanation, never a sum.

After *Suppose this is true* the reader sees the ending's number re-worked in a
world where the supposition holds, beside an edge computed from the world where
nothing was supposed. These are the terms relating the two: the map's own
chance of the supposition times the reading where it holds, plus one minus that
chance times the reading where it does not.

**The two terms do not add up to the unsupposed number and nothing here claims
they do.** A cause of the supposed claim may reach the ending another way, and
supposing something pins a **date** as well as a truth while the unsupposed
world averages over the days it might have happened. So these are four numbers
shown term by term, and nothing computes an edge from them.

reading_otherwise.description: The ending's likelihood where that same claim goes the other way.

reading_supposed.description: The ending's likelihood in the world the reader is looking at.

says.description: What these terms are, and what they are not.
says.title: Says

weight_otherwise.description: One minus it. The two always sum to one.

weight_supposed.description: The map's own chance of that claim coming out the way they supposed it.

MixtureShown.title: MixtureShown

NotPriced.description:
What is priced in, where an edge could not be built — a named refusal and a break-even.

A refusal is a value and never a blank. Where the ending names a contract, the
break-even comes with it, because it needs no quote and is the honest answer
when there is none. Where the ending names an instrument, the break-even is a
**price** rather than a likelihood, and the reader's own entry price is what
makes it computable.

because.description: Which of the four refusals this is.
because.title: Because

buy_below.description: Worth buying below this, where the ending names a contract.

costs_are_unknown.description: Said out loud where nobody has stated what it costs to get in and out of the instrument, so the price above is the entry price itself.
costs_are_unknown.title: Costs Are Unknown

fee.description: The venue's fee, where anybody has read it. Nothing at all where nobody has.

fee_is_unknown.description: Said out loud where nobody has read the fee schedule; nothing otherwise.
fee_is_unknown.title: Fee Is Unknown

price_break_even.description: The price at which a position in an instrument is worth nothing: the reader's own entry price moved by what it costs to get in and out. Nothing at all where the ending names a contract, which has a break-even in likelihoods instead.

sell_above.description: Worth selling above this, where the ending names a contract.

sentence.description: What the card prints, in plain words a reader can act on.
sentence.title: Sentence

NotPriced.title: NotPriced

NotRanked.description:
One tradeable ending the ranking leaves out, and why.

Said out loud rather than quietly missing, because *this ending is not ranked*
and *this ending was never considered* are different facts and a reader can act
on only one of them.

because.description: Which of the three reasons it was.
because.title: Because

sentence.description: What the card prints beside it.
sentence.title: Sentence

NotRanked.title: NotRanked

PricedIn.description:
What is priced in, where a venue quotes this claim and an edge could be built.

The card shows whichever side is worth taking. When neither is, that is a
complete answer rather than a gap: the number this side pays on sits inside the
venue's own bid and offer with fees paid.

buy_below.description: Worth buying at any offer below this.

buying.description: What buying is worth, at the offer, after the fee.

fee.description: What the venue charges on one filled trade, in the same units as a price. Nothing at all means nobody has read the venue's schedule, which is not the same as a fee of nothing.

fee_is_unknown.description: Said out loud where nobody has read the fee schedule; nothing otherwise.
fee_is_unknown.title: Fee Is Unknown

headline.description: Which side the card leads with, or that neither is worth taking.
headline.title: Headline

mixture.description: The terms relating a supposed reading to this one, where the reader supposed something and the other world was worked out. An explanation that never computes the edge. Nothing at all otherwise.

model.description: The claim's own likelihood — the chance it comes true — read from the map with nothing fixed by an edit.

not_headlined_because.description: Why a positive edge is not led with: the gap is narrower than the venue's smallest price step, or it is inside the model's own stated range.
not_headlined_because.title: Not Headlined Because

pays_on.description: The likelihood this side of the contract actually pays on. The same number on a yes side; one minus it, range turned over, on a no side.

quote.description: The venue's two prices and the day they were read.

sell_above.description: Worth selling at any bid above this.

selling.description: What selling is worth, at the bid, after the fee.

PricedIn.title: PricedIn

QuotedPrices.description:
What a venue is showing, and when it was read.

A price the reader typed is **theirs**, not a venue's: it is their report of a
price they believe they could deal at, and it never fills the market's slot. So
the three figures below are owned by a venue on a quote a venue gave and by the
reader on one they typed, and the card says which on the same line as the
number.

bid.description: The best bid: the price you would sell at.

how.description: How it reached us: read now, read from a committed file, or typed.
how.title: How

midpoint.description: Halfway between the two, shown because a reader recognises it and never traded at.

offer.description: The best offer: the price you would buy at.

venue.description: Which venue published it, or that the reader entered it.
venue.title: Venue

QuotedPrices.title: QuotedPrices

RankedEnding.description: One tradeable ending in the ranking, and which rule put it there.

headline.description: Whether this row may be led with, or only listed.
headline.title: Headline

instrument.description: What would be bought or sold, or the contract's identifier.
instrument.title: Instrument

key.description: The number that rule ranked it on.

made_of.description: The numbers the key is made of, so it can say why it is what it is.
made_of.title: Made Of

not_headlined_because.description: Why it may not be led with. Nothing where it may.
not_headlined_because.title: Not Headlined Because

ranked_by.description: Which of the two rules ranked this row. Never a blend of the two.
ranked_by.title: Ranked By

trades.description: Whether it names something traded or a contract.
trades.title: Trades

RankedEnding.title: RankedEnding

RiskExit.description:
What the reader typed about getting out, and how often each end is reached first.

The size their risk budget implies and the greyed ceiling are **not** here:
they are on the leg, because a leg has to be complete on its own.

first_touch_refused.description: Why there is no first touch here. Nothing where the shares were worked out.
first_touch_refused.title: First Touch Refused

horizon.description: The day by which they expect to be out.
horizon.title: Horizon

method.description: How the shares were arrived at.
method.title: Method

neither.description: How often the window closes with neither touched. The three sum to one.

risk_budget.description: The share of capital they are prepared to lose here.

stop.description: The price at which they get out for a loss. Never derived.

stop_at.description: The level actually checked for the stop, after the barrier shift.

stop_first.description: How often the stop is touched before the target, over the drawn worlds.

target.description: The price at which they get out for a gain. Never derived.

target_first.description: How often the target is touched first.

through.description: How many days of the window the shares were read to: the reader's own horizon, counted from the day the window opened. Shares over a window nobody named are numbers nobody can check.

RiskExit.title: RiskExit

ShockExported.description:
A shock the reader placed, with its probability written down as nothing at all.

The field exists and is fixed at nothing. An absent field reads as an
oversight; a field that says *null* says that nobody claims to know, which is
the truth: the reader supposed this, and supposing something is not a statement
about how likely it is.

change_to_the_position.description: What the position is worth on that branch less what it is worth without it.

name.description: What they supposed, in their own words.
name.title: Name

placed_by.description: Who placed it. Always the reader.
placed_by.title: Placed By

probability.description: Always nothing at all. A shock is supposed, not forecast, and this document will not carry a number here.
probability.title: Probability

says.description: Why there is no probability here.
says.title: Says

ShockExported.title: ShockExported

Stamp.description:
The three things a card can be rebuilt from, plus the day it was worked out for.

A world is a computed result and never a source of truth: it can always be
thrown away and rebuilt from the base map, the branch and the seed. Stamping
them here is what makes the document replayable rather than merely readable.

as_of.description: The first day of the window the numbers were worked out over.
as_of.title: As Of

base_id.description: The map this was built from.
base_id.title: Base Id

branch_id.description: The branch folded on, or nothing at all for the untouched map.
branch_id.title: Branch Id

seed.description: The one number every random draw behind this came from.
seed.title: Seed

Stamp.title: Stamp

TailRow.description: One tail: unlikely, and enough to hurt. Never averaged into anything.

harm.description: What it would do to the position, as a loss.

likelihood.description: The model's own chance of it, range and all.

what_could_be_done.description: What a reader could do about it, or why nothing can.
what_could_be_done.title: What Could Be Done

TailRow.title: TailRow

TakesYouOutRow.description:
One claim over-represented in the worlds where the stop went first.

**Company, not cause.** A claim can be over-represented in the worlds that
stopped the reader out because it shares a cause with whatever did. The map
beside the card is where the mechanism lives.

came_on.description: The share of all the drawn worlds where it came on at all.

came_on_first.description: The share of the stop-first worlds where this claim had already come on before the stop was touched, with the interval on that share.

coverage.description: How often the interval on the share above is meant to cover its true share. A figure rather than words inside a sentence, so that it cannot be printed without saying whose number it is.

days_before_the_stop.description: The typical days between this claim coming on and the stop being touched. **Nothing at all** where no drawn world had it come on before the stop, which is an absence and never a day count of nothing.

draws.description: How many equally-weighted worlds the share above is worth.

lift.description: How much more often this claim had already come on where the stop went first than it came on across all the drawn worlds. Three means three times as often; one means it tells you nothing. No interval, because no coverage is claimed for a ratio of two shares over overlapping sets.

no_days_because.description: Why there is no day count, in plain words. Nothing where there is one.
no_days_because.title: No Days Because

TakesYouOutRow.title: TakesYouOutRow

can_be_seen.description: Whether anybody publishes the answer at all.
can_be_seen.title: Can Be Seen

why.description: Why it cannot be watched for.
why.title: Why

points.description: How much of the shift this claim accounts for.

WhatElseCanITrade.description:
Every tradeable ending on the map, ranked — by two rules, kept apart.

Two lists rather than one because an edge in cents and a move in per cent are
not the same quantity and there is no honest exchange rate between them. Each
list is ordered within itself; no row is ever ordered against a row in the
other.

by_the_shift_times_the_move.description: Endings naming an instrument, largest shift times move first.
by_the_shift_times_the_move.title: By The Shift Times The Move

by_the_size_of_its_edge.description: Endings a venue quotes, best edge first, whichever side it favours.
by_the_size_of_its_edge.title: By The Size Of Its Edge

not_ranked.description: Tradeable endings neither rule could rank, each with its reason.
not_ranked.title: Not Ranked

two_rules.description: Why there are two lists, said on the card itself.
two_rules.title: Two Rules

WhatElseCanITrade.title: WhatElseCanITrade

floor.description: The fewest equally-weighted worlds a row may rest on.

left_off.description: Every claim the rail leaves off, with its reason, in full sentences.

rows.description: The claims, ranked by lift, highest first. Empty where the draws are too few.

stop_first_worlds.description: How many drawn worlds ended with the stop touched first, before weighting.

too_few_draws.description: Why the rail is empty, where it is empty because the draws behind it are too few. An empty rail without this reads as *nothing takes you out*.
